title: Ben Webster and other players adopt the Chinese cymbal sound
summary: Ben Webster loved the rivet cymbal, and Dizzy Gillespie and Kenny Dorham later had drummers use one; Leeman says it suits tenor sax.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Was Ben in Charlie Barnet's band?
Well, I'm trying to say how did he get to be --

Well, I worked with Ben after Woody Herman, I'll have to get to that -- but that's one of the reasons that he wanted -- every time I wasn't with Ben Webster, when he had a little group of his own, he told the drummer, and the drummer would come running to me and say, "Gee, what kind of a cymbal is that that Ben keeps talking about?" and I'd say it's a Chinese cymbal with rivets, and Ben doesn't want to play behind anything else -- I think Sonny Greer had spoiled him.
Do you know that Dizzy Gillespie won't have a drummer unless he has that?
Yes, Dizzy was with Charlie Barnet for awhile. He came from Cab's band.
All of the great jazz instrumentalists nowadays buy their own Chinese cymbals so that you have --
Dizzy had his own so we'd have it.
Yeah, I think that's nice to know, Cliff, that you ...
Kenny Dorham bought a couple, and he takes them.
And Bobby Rosengarden has a sizzle cymbal now, but originally Kenny took it around to the different drummers, and said, 'Hey, play this for me.'

It's nice to know that it became so prevalent because of you that they don't even demand their drummers to have it, they buy it and say to their drummers 'play this' and when they change drummers, they keep the cymbal so that whatever the next drummer comes in, it's ...
It seems to be such a right sound, if it's a good cymbal and it is tacked properly with a good touch on it, it seems to be such a right sound for tenor saxophone.
Over the years I have replaced the Chinese cymbal, but I use the sizzle cymbal at times to take its place -- it's not a sizzle cymbal, but a cymbal with sizzles in it, as to play color.
